Overview
Englert - Director of Manufacturing
As the Director of Manufacturing, you will lead daily operations and drives sustained performance across Safety, Quality, Delivery, Cost, and People. Reporting to the President of Manufacturing, this role partners with Quality, Maintenance, Engineering/Continuous Improvement, Supply Chain, Production Planning, and other support functions to achieve plant objectives.
This leader is accountable for production performance, labor productivity, schedule attainment, manufacturing cost, capacity utilization, talent development, and continuous improvement. The role establishes disciplined shop-floor management, develops manufacturing leaders, and builds a culture of accountability, problem solving, teamwork, and operational excellence.
Pay Range: Starting at $130,000 per year with variable comp
Responsibilities
Lead daily manufacturing operations to meet or exceed targets for Safety, Quality, Delivery, Cost, Productivity, and People.
Convert forecasts, demand, and business priorities into manufacturing plans, staffing models, capacity requirements, and execution priorities.
Lead, coach, and develop manufacturing managers, supervisors, and frontline leaders with clear expectations, accountability, and performance standards.
Maintain a disciplined daily management system with shift meetings, production reviews, KPI boards, escalation routines, and corrective-action follow-up.
Monitor manufacturing KPIs including safety performance, schedule attainment, output, labor efficiency, overtime, scrap, rework, downtime, productivity, and manufacturing cost.
Ensure production issues and performance gaps are quickly identified, root causes addressed, corrective actions assigned, and results sustained.
Partner with Quality to improve first-pass yield, reduce defects and rework, resolve customer concerns, and strengthen process controls.
Partner with Maintenance to improve equipment reliability, reduce unplanned downtime, strengthen preventive maintenance, and increase asset utilization.
Collaborate with Production Planning and Supply Chain to align schedules, material availability, inventory needs, and customer commitments.
Partner with Engineering and Continuous Improvement to improve productivity, capacity, material flow, ergonomics, quality, and manufacturing cost.
Drive Lean Manufacturing and continuous improvement through standard work, 5S/6S, visual management, problem solving, waste elimination, line balancing, and process optimization.
Increase output and capacity utilization while reducing labor hours, overtime, scrap, rework, downtime, and operational waste.
Establish, document, train, audit, and sustain standardized work processes and operating procedures.
Develop capacity and labor plans that support current demand, growth initiatives, new products, and changing customer requirements.
Use ERP systems and operational data to analyze performance, identify trends, set priorities, and drive factbased decisions.
Maintain daily, weekly, and monthly reporting that compares results to targets and highlights trends, gaps, and corrective actions.
Support the annual operating plan, manufacturing budget, capital requirements, productivity initiatives, and cost-reduction targets.
Manage manufacturing expenses within budget and deliver year-over-year improvements in labor productivity, conversion cost, scrap, and operational efficiency.
Champion safety by ensuring compliance with standards, participation in safety initiatives, and proactive risk identification and elimination.
Ensure manufacturing operations comply with company policies, regulatory requirements, quality systems, environmental requirements, and operating procedures.
Build succession plans and strengthen the leadership pipeline through coaching, performance management, cross-training, and talent development.
Partner with Human Resources to support hiring, onboarding, training, and retention of manufacturing employees and leaders.
Foster a culture where employees identify problems, recommend improvements, and engage in continuous improvement.
Perform other duties and lead special projects as assigned by the Sr. Director of Manufacturing Operations.
Qualifications
Key Performance Indicators
Success Will Be Measured By Sustained Improvement In
Safety performance
First-pass yield and internal quality
Customer quality and manufacturing-related complaints
Schedule attainment and on-time completion
Labor productivity and efficiency
Overtime
Scrap and rework
Equipment downtime and capacity utilization
Manufacturing cost
Inventory and material flow
Continuous improvement savings
Employee development, engagement, and retention
Skills, Knowledge, And Abilities
Manufacturing Leadership: Proven ability to lead complex manufacturing operations and deliver results through execution, accountability, and disciplined follow-through.
Operational Excellence: Strong command of manufacturing systems, production management, standard work, capacity planning, labor optimization, and performance management.
Lean Manufacturing & Continuous Improvement: Ability to apply Lean principles and structured problem solving to eliminate waste, improve flow, increase productivity, and reduce cost.
Financial Acumen: Strong understanding of manufacturing cost, labor performance, budgeting, productivity, capital investment, and plant profitability drivers.
Data-Driven Decision Making: Ability to use ERP systems, KPIs, dashboards, and financial data to identify trends, prioritize opportunities, and drive corrective action.
People Leadership: Proven ability to coach, develop, and hold leaders accountable while building a highperformance, respectful, and collaborative culture.
Cross-Functional Collaboration: Ability to work effectively with Quality, Maintenance, Supply Chain, Engineering, Continuous Improvement, Finance, Human Resources, Sales, and other partners.
Problem Solving: Strong analytical skills with demonstrated use of structured root-cause analysis and corrective-action methods.
Change Leadership: Ability to lead organizational and operational changes while building ownership and accountability across manufacturing.
Shop-Floor Leadership: Hands-on leadership style with consistent floor presence and direct engagement with employees, supervisors, and operations.
Education And Experience
Bachelor’s degree in engineering, business or related field required; equivalent education and significant manufacturing leadership experience may be considered.
Minimum 7–10 years of progressive manufacturing experience, including at least five years in manufacturing leadership.
Experience managing multi-shift manufacturing operations and leading managers and supervisors.
Strong background in Lean Manufacturing, continuous improvement, structured problem solving, and performance management.
Experience using ERP/MRP systems and manufacturing data to manage performance and guide operational decisions.
Experience managing manufacturing budgets, labor productivity, cost reduction, and operational improvement programs.
Experience working within formal safety and quality management systems.
Lean Six Sigma Green Belt or equivalent practical continuous improvement experience preferred.
MBA, advanced technical degree, or Lean Six Sigma Black Belt preferred.
Bilingual Spanish preffered
Leadership Expectations
The Director of Manufacturing must be a visible shop-floor leader who creates accountability, develops leaders, and prevents recurring operational issues.
The successful leader will establish disciplined operating routines, use data to guide decisions, challenge existing processes, and continuously improve safety, quality, delivery, productivity, and cost.
This role works with the Sr. Director of Manufacturing Operations and leaders across Quality, Maintenance, Supply Chain, Engineering/Continuous Improvement, Finance, and Human Resources to achieve site and business objectives.
Physical Requirements
Prolonged standing and walking.
Must be able to lift 50 to 100 pounds and additional weight with assistance.
The physical demands described are representative of those required to perform the essential functions of this role. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform these functions.
Benefits
Major Medical, Dental, Vision, 401(k), Flexible Time Off (FTO), Quarterly Bonus, advancement opportunities, and additional perks.
By submitting your application, you agree that it may be shared with Great Day affiliated companies for consideration.
Englert Inc. and its subsidiaries and affiliates, including LeafGuard Holdings, provide equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants and prohibit discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local law.

We are seeking a highly skilled, hands-on Engineering Manager to lead our engineering function in a fast-paced precision manufacturing environment. ** The Site Quality Manager is responsible for leading all aspects of the Quality Management Program for a multi-billion-dollar data center campus construction project.
This position provides strategic and operational leadership to ensure construction, testing, commissioning, and turnover activities are executed in compliance with project requirements, client standards, applicable codes, contractual obligations, and Fluor quality processes.
The Site Quality Manager serves as the primary quality representative for the project and works closely with the client, engineering, procurement, construction, commissioning, and trade contractor organizations to drive quality performance across the entire project lifecycle.

...

* Lead the implementation, execution, and continuous improvement of the Project Quality Management System for a large-scale data center construction program.
* Develop and execute project-specific quality strategies that support safe, efficient, and defect-free construction and turnover.
* Manage, mentor, and develop a multidisciplinary team of quality professionals including quality engineers, inspectors, document control personnel, and subcontractor quality representatives.
* Establish clear quality expectations and accountability across all project participants, including Fluor personnel, subcontractors, suppliers, and commissioning teams.
* Serve as the primary quality interface with the client, participating in executive reviews, quality leadership meetings, audits, and project performance discussions.
* Ensure compliance with contract requirements, client data center standards, engineering specifications, applicable building codes, industry standards, and regulatory requirements.
* Oversee implementation of Inspection and Test Plans (ITPs), quality surveillance programs, audit programs, and quality verification activities.
* Lead quality planning efforts for critical mission-critical systems including electrical distribution, substations, generators, UPS systems, battery systems, switchgear, network infrastructure, mechanical cooling systems, fire protection, and building automation systems.
* Ensure quality requirements are effectively integrated into procurement, fabrication, installation, testing, commissioning, and turnover processes.
* Direct the management of nonconformance reporting, corrective actions, root cause analysis, and lessons learned programs.

...

* Ensure project turnover documentation, quality records, testing documentation, and commissioning packages meet client and contractual requirements.
* Drive digital quality initiatives and effective use of project quality management systems, reporting tools, and turnover platforms.

...

* Accredited four (4) degree or global equivalent in applicable field of study and sixteen (16) years of work-related experience or a combination of education and directly related experience equal to twenty (20) years if non-degreed; some locations may have additional or different qualifications in order to comply with local regulations
* Ability to communicate effectively with audiences that include but are not limited to management, coworkers, clients, vendors, contractors, and other stakeholders
* Job related technical knowledge necessary to complete the job
* Ability to learn and apply knowledge of applicable local, state/province, and federal/national statutes and guidelines

...

* Demonstrated experience leading quality programs on large-scale industrial, advanced technology, mission-critical, semiconductor, pharmaceutical, manufacturing, infrastructure, or data center construction projects.
* Experience managing quality organizations supporting projects exceeding $1 billion in total installed cost.
* Strong understanding of mission-critical systems construction, testing, commissioning, and turnover methodologies.
* Knowledge of applicable quality management principles, including ISO 9001 and industry best practices.
* Experience leading contractor quality audits, supplier assessments, surveillance programs, and corrective action processes.
* Proven ability to interface effectively with executive client leadership and senior project stakeholders.
* Experience utilizing digital quality management and turnover systems.
* Ability to analyze quality performance metrics and implement continuous improvement initiatives.
* Drive development of the safety culture on the project.

...

**Preferred Qualifications
**
* ASQ Certified Quality Manager (CMQ/OE), Certified Quality Engineer (CQE), or equivalent certification.
* Previous experience on hyperscale or enterprise data center projects.
* Experience supporting integrated commissioning and systems completion programs.
* Strong knowledge of electrical and mechanical systems associated with mission-critical facilities.
